newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stock fall not due to foreigner selling -Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Stock fall not due to foreigner selling -Sakakibara.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Monday that he did not think a decline in Tokyo stocks was caused by foreign investors' selling.
Sakakibara said selling of Japanese shares by foreigners amounted to 61.5 billion yen in January, while selling by Japanese brokerage firms from their own accounts amounted to 436.9 billion yen.
"Foreign selling is extremely small. I don't think share prices moved because of this," Sakakibara told the budget committee of the Lower House of parliament.
